\section{Normative definitions and boundary}
\label{sec:definitions}

\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
\item[SCI-JINC observation estimator.]
A signed spatial-kernel transformer that consumes exact PTC signal occurrences
and their exact AST coordinates and forms at most one complete JINC bundle for
each admitted and requested stable array in one observation.  It is a sibling
alternative to ordinary SCI-MAP, not a downstream stage of SCI-MAP.

\item[Exact occurrence.]
The scientific identity that jointly fixes observation, detector occurrence
and UID, stable RTC output sample, PTC product and application generation, PTC
segment, stable array/group, time attribute, and immutable parent chain.  Row
position, nearest time, tolerance, shape, detector order, or numerical equality
is not a substitute.

\item[Exact AST association.]
The relation binding $z_i$ to the AST-owned
\texttt{SCI-AST:rtc\_output\_grid\_coordinates@1} continuous coordinate for the
same processed sample realization in the exact target JINC WCS.  Its data-model
join is an engineering choice; its scientific identity is not.

\item[JINC sample admission.]
The decision of the immutable
\texttt{SCI-JINC:jinc\_map\_contribution@1} profile that one exact upstream
occurrence may be considered by JINC.  It neither implies rounded-center
domain admission nor pixel support.

\item[Rounded-center domain admission.]
The JINC-owned occurrence-level gate applied after center rounding and before
any footprint evaluation.  The resolved rounded center must lie within the
finite destination pixel domain.  An outside center makes $I_{ip}=0$ for every
$p$, even when the square footprint would overlap the map.

\item[Point phase.]
The single-valued residual between the exact continuous sample coordinate and
the resolved rounded center, quantized on each axis to select one
point-evaluated kernel matrix.  It is not a pixel-area average.

\item[Square support.]
The fully populated square cache whose half-width is fixed by $(r_{\max})_a$.
Every resolved square pixel is evaluated, including corners with radius larger
than $(r_{\max})_a$; there is no circular membership predicate.

\item[Sample-pixel membership.]
The Boolean proposition $I_{ip}=1$ after sample admission, exact coordinate
association, rounded-center domain admission, square placement, finite local
geometry, and every pixel-local precondition.  A contract-defined analytic
zero is a member with zero contribution; outside support is nonmembership; a
finite negative coefficient is an ordinary signed member.

\item[Local formal support.]
The state in which the required inputs and accumulators are finite, $Q_p>0$,
$C_p\ne0$, and cancellation is resolved with total numerical error negligible
relative to the approximately $10^{-3}$ instrument-fidelity scale.  A named
empirical policy may narrow this state but never promote it.

\item[Complete observation bundle.]
The atomic fixed-role product for one observation, stable array, exact JINC
plan and realization, target WCS, and lifecycle generation.  It contains
exactly $N_p$, $C_p$, $Q_p$, derived $m_p$ with local support/validity, and
$T_p^{(\kappa^2)}$.

\item[Whole-bundle failure.]
Failure to form or publish any required whole-product role.  It suppresses the
affected bundle without a partial role, placeholder, synthetic empty-array
product, or completion override.  Pixel-local invalid support is ordinary
bundle content and is not whole-bundle failure.

\item[Typed numerical unavailability.]
The fail-closed state in which a numerical JINC route cannot be realized
because an exact authorized TolTEC kernel parameter set or an exact registered,
selected, realized, JINC-permitted PTC coefficient family/payload is absent.
It is not repaired by a hidden default, unity coefficient, alternate family,
ordinary MAP permission, inherited scale, or implementation value.

\item[Scientific destination identity.]
The product identity formed from observation, stable array, exact JINC plan and
realization, target WCS, product role, and lifecycle generation.  Worker,
thread, process, container, filename, vector position, and network order are
not scientific identity.
\end{description}
